source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1964, p. 2 ("Taylor-Nobbs' success: Castlereagh"); Belfast Telegraph, 11 June 1964, p. 13 ("Castlereagh Rural District Council: notice of result")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: The Castlereagh results report read in the Belfast News-Letter of 5 June 1964; Dundonald and Gilnahirk counts from the returning officer's notice in the Belfast Telegraph of 11 June 1964. Name read on the BNA image of the returning officer's notice (council-audit, Nov 2026).

note: Triennial election of Castlereagh Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Seven of the nine divisions were contested, Craigavad and Holywood returning unopposed. The counts for Dundonald and Gilnahirk are not printed in the report read and those divisions are omitted. Returned unopposed. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Corrected from the page image of the Belfast Telegraph, 11 June 1964, p. 13 (council-audit, Nov 2026): the returning officer's notice of result prints BOYD, Thomas Henry, elected unopposed for Holywood Rural (was entered as B. Boyd, not found on the cited News-Letter page); the name now takes the form of the 1967 round (Thomas H. Boyd) and the notice is cited first. Renamed from 'Holywood' to Holywood Rural (w8-redirects, Nov 2026): the Belfast Telegraph's notice of result, 11 June 1964, p. 13, heads the division Holywood Rural, the name the 1961 and 1967 rounds file. The old address (holywood) answers with a redirect to this one.
